LESSON: SIGN READING 1.2.1 EXTENSIVE SIGN READING USE OF REFERENCE MATERIALS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Sign Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading Use of Reference Materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading Use of Reference Materials, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: what they have sign read. (Ensure the seating arrangement supports equal access to signed information). 1. Why do you read and sign read books?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading Use of Reference Materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: Interacting with technology as learners manipulate electronic reference materials.

• Learning to Learn: Learning independently as learners sign read selected reference materials independently.

Values:
• Unity: Cooperation as the learner reports and discusses what they have read in small groups

• Responsibility: Hardwork as the learner visits a library to select reading materials and read independently

Link to other Subjects:

The learner uses the skill to use reference materials in all the other learning areas as they all require searching for information.

Suggested learning resources:

reference materials such as English dictionaries, Sign Language dictionaries ,junior encyclopaedias, and subject-specific encyclopaedias Pictures and photographs,
